text_blocks.content: 📍 Legion Outpost Theta-7 - Command Chamber

The Legion outpost was carved into the side of a basalt cliff, all sharp angles and reinforced dream-warding runes. Silas waited in the command chamber, his boots clicking on polished obsidian floors. The air smelled of ozone and cold stone.
A broken Anchorstone fragment sat on a display pedestal in the center of the room, glowing with a sickly, intermittent light. Cracks spiderwebbed across its surface.
They're displaying it like a trophy. Not a relic to be studied, but evidence of enemy action.
The heavy iron door slid open with a hydraulic hiss.
Captain Rourke Hale entered, followed by two stone-faced legionnaires. Hale's uniform was immaculate, but his eyes held the same haunted look Silas saw in every mirror.
Reed. Your report mentioned engineered fractures. Show me.
Silas laid the charcoal rubbing on the command table. The three sigils formed a perfect triangle around the fracture point.
This wasn't natural erosion, Captain. Someone carved these. The design suggests Anchorstone engineering knowledge. Whoever did this knew exactly where the Veil would fray at dawn.
Hale studied the rubbing, his expression unreadable. The two legionnaires exchanged a glance.
You're certain it's not dream-scarring? Residual Oneiros energy can sometimes manifest as patterns.
Positive. The scorch marks are physical, not psychic. And the pattern repeats—three points, ritual geometry. This was intentional sabotage.
Hale nodded slowly, then tapped the command tablet on his wrist. A holographic map shimmered into existence above the table.
The map showed a dozen red markers scattered across the Shifting Weald—all fracture points. Three of them formed a perfect triangle matching Silas's rubbing.
We've been tracking these for weeks. Your confirmation is... inconvenient.
Inconvenient? Not 'alarming.' Not 'a crisis.' Inconvenient.
Captain, if someone's deliberately weakening the Veil—
We know who. The Court of Echoing Whispers. Dream-entities trying to tear down the barrier. Your discovery confirms their methods, not their existence.
Hale zoomed the map to show a larger pattern. The triangle was just one of several geometric formations across the region.
But here's what concerns us more, Reed. The sigil design. Anchorstone engineering. That knowledge is restricted to Veil Wardens and senior Legion engineers.
A low hum began to emanate from the broken Anchorstone fragment, growing in intensity.
Which means either the Wardens are compromised... or we have a traitor in our ranks.
Silas felt the room tilt. The Legion's paranoia wasn't just directed outward. It was turning inward, a snake eating its own tail.
Your orders, Reed. You'll return to the Weald. Not to seal fractures—to observe. Watch who comes to inspect your work. Report any Veil Warden activity directly to me, bypassing standard channels.
Hale's eyes locked on Silas. 'Bypassing standard channels' meant Lyra Vance wouldn't see the reports.
They want me to spy on the Wardens. Not investigate the sabotage, but gather evidence against them.
Captain, if the Wardens are involved in the sabotage, shouldn't we—
Our priority is identifying the rot within. The fractures are symptoms, Reed. We're treating the disease.
The Anchorstone fragment pulsed once, violently, then fell dark.
Hale turned away, the conversation clearly over. The two legionnaires stepped forward, their presence suddenly feeling less like protection and more like containment.
New faction tension: Legion priorities shifting from external defense to internal purge
